subject.title: refactor(plugin-sdk): isolate core session state from plugin mutations

question: Should OpenClaw preserve or version the shipped `getAcpSessionManager()` class-identity contract while adding the restricted facade, or intentionally accept an immediate breaking replacement to enforce the isolation boundary?
rationale: The patch closes a legitimate plugin-to-core escape path, but choosing whether that security boundary justifies breaking a shipped Plugin SDK identity contract requires explicit owner intent.

options.title: Stage a versioned facade
options.body: Add a new structural facade API and retain or deprecate the shipped getter with migration documentation and compatibility tests.

options.title: Approve the breaking replacement
options.body: Accept the identity break explicitly and require documented upgrade impact plus installed-plugin migration proof.

options.title: Pause for a preserving design
options.body: Hold the PR until isolation can be enforced without changing the shipped getter identity.

recommendation.title: Stage a versioned facade
recommendation.body: Add a new structural facade API and retain or deprecate the shipped getter with migration documentation and compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is the best available adjacent ACP/plugin product-decision candidate, though exact code ownership remains unverified.
